Donepezil Hydrochloride: Research began at Eisai in 1983 under Hachiro Sugimoto; now the most widely used drug for Alzheimer's disease. First approval/introduction: US FDA 1996 (Eisai; co-marketed with Pfizer). Memantine Hydrochloride: First synthesised by Eli Lilly in 1963 as an antidiabetic agent; Merz discovered its CNS activity in 1972 and developed it for dementia. First approval/introduction: Germany 1989 (Merz Pharma); EU 2002; US FDA 2003.
Donepezil 5 mg + Memantine 5 mg; Donepezil 5 mg + Memantine 10 mg

Donepezil increases cholinergic neurotransmission; memantine reduces glutamate excitotoxicity. Combined therapy provides additive benefit in cognition, function and behaviour in moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease.

Donepezil Hydrochloride Reversible, selective inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase in the CNS, increasing acetylcholine concentrations at cholinergic synapses and improving cognition in Alzheimer's disease. Receptor / target profile: Reversible, selective acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; also a potent sigma-1 receptor agonist with possible neuroprotective effects.

Memantine Hydrochloride Moderate-affinity, voltage-dependent uncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist; blocks pathologically elevated glutamate activity that may cause neuronal dysfunction, while allowing physiological signalling. Receptor / target profile: Low-affinity, voltage-dependent uncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist that blocks pathological excitotoxicity while preserving normal synaptic transmission.

Donepezil Hydrochloride: Heart rate; weight; GI bleeding signs; cognitive response at 3–6 months.
Memantine Hydrochloride: Renal function; urine pH changes; BP.

Donepezil Hydrochloride: Cholinergic crisis: nausea, vomiting, salivation, sweating, bradycardia, hypotension, respiratory depression, convulsions, muscle weakness. Atropine titrated to effect; supportive care. Memantine Hydrochloride: Restlessness, psychosis, visual hallucinations, somnolence, stupor, loss of consciousness. Supportive care; urine acidification may enhance elimination.
Tariot et al., JAMA 2004 – adding memantine to stable donepezil improved cognition and function in moderate–severe Alzheimer's.
DOMINO-AD (Howard et al., NEJM 2012) – continuing donepezil in moderate–severe disease was beneficial.
Take at bedtime (vivid dreams – switch to morning if troublesome)
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
